titulo: The dish you were never going to order
subtitulo: Cosa mi consiglia is the shortest route to the thing the kitchen is actually proud of
cena: The menu has forty items, you recognise six, and you are about to order the sixth one for the fourth night running.
frasePiso: Stop reading the menu. Ask the person who knows what came in this morning.
decisao: pedir o que a casa recomenda em vez do prato que você já reconhece, que é a diferença entre comer na Itália e comer o que você comeria em casa

steps.pt: Four nights of the dish you already knew is the most common way to eat badly in a country that eats extremely well.
One sentence solves it. Cosa mi consiglia — what do you recommend. Ask it before you have read anything.

steps.promptPt: Put the menu down and ask. Speak now.

steps.acao: Take the first thing they name. That is the one the kitchen is proud of today.
steps.es: Oggi abbiamo i carciofi. Li facciamo alla giudia.
steps.pt: Today we have artichokes. We do them Jewish-style.
steps.tts: Oggi abbiamo i carciofi. Li facciamo alla giudia.

steps.promptPt: Take the recommendation without asking three follow-up questions. Speak now.
steps.pt: Then I'll have that, I trust you.
Mi fido — I trust you — is the two words that change the answer you get for the rest of the meal.

steps.promptPt: Ask for the local dish specifically, using the frame from B08. Speak now.
steps.es: C'è un piatto tipico di qui?
steps.pinyin: cheh oon pee-AT-to TEE-pee-ko dee kwee
steps.pt: Is there a dish typical of here?
steps.tts: C'è un piatto tipico di qui?

steps.pt: The menu is in courses: antipasto, primo, secondo, contorno, dolce. You do not have to order all five, and almost nobody does.

steps.promptPt: Order two courses and say so, so nothing else arrives. Speak now.
steps.es: Solo un primo e un contorno, grazie.
steps.pinyin: SO-lo oon PREE-mo eh oon kon-TOR-no, GRA-tsee-eh
steps.pt: Just a first course and a side, thank you.
steps.tts: Solo un primo e un contorno, grazie.

steps.promptPt: Ask what today's dish is — the one not printed on the menu. Speak now.
steps.es: Qual è il piatto del giorno?
steps.pinyin: kwal eh eel pee-AT-to del JOR-no
steps.tts: Qual è il piatto del giorno?

steps.promptPt: You do not know what a word on the menu is. Ask, without apologising. Speak now.

steps.acao: If it is offal or something unfamiliar, that is information, not a warning. Decide, do not flinch.
steps.es: È la trippa. Piatto povero, ma buonissimo.
steps.pt: It's tripe. A poor man's dish, but delicious.
steps.tts: È la trippa. Piatto povero, ma buonissimo.

steps.promptPt: Let them pick the wine too. Ask for the house one. Speak now.
steps.es: Un quarto di vino della casa, rosso.
steps.pinyin: oon KWAR-to dee VEE-no DEL-la KA-za, ROS-so
steps.pt: A quarter litre of house wine, red.
steps.tts: Un quarto di vino della casa, rosso.

steps.promptPt: They ask about dessert. Ask what is made in-house. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you make the dessert yourselves?

steps.es: Cosa mi consiglia? Allora prendo quello, mi fido. Un quarto di vino della casa, rosso.
steps.pinyin: KO-za mee kon-SEE-lya. al-LO-ra PREN-do KWEL-lo mee FEE-do. oon KWAR-to dee VEE-no DEL-la KA-za ROS-so
steps.pt: Shadow the handover: ask, accept, and let them choose the wine.
steps.tts: Cosa mi consiglia? Allora prendo quello, mi fido. Un quarto di vino della casa, rosso.

steps.pt: I03 done. Cosa mi consiglia, mi fido, and the house wine — three moves that hand the meal to someone who knows.

secoes.titulo: Cosa mi consiglia, then mi fido
secoes.corpo: The first sentence gets a recommendation; the second gets the good one. Accepting without negotiation signals that you are not going to be a difficult table, and the quality of what arrives reflects that.

exemplos.pt: Then I'll have that, I trust you.

secoes.titulo: You do not order every course
secoes.corpo: Antipasto, primo, secondo, contorno, dolce is the full structure, not the expected order. A primo and a contorno is a completely normal meal, and saying which courses you want up front stops the rest from arriving.

A fixed multilingual menu with photographs, a range spanning pizza, pasta, sushi and burgers, and someone working the pavement to bring you in are the documented markers of a place built around never seeing you again. Note that a menù del giorno is a different thing entirely and is a good sign. The positive counter-signal is a menu written in Italian, sometimes with dialect words, listing regional dishes rather than a national greatest-hits list.

House wine sold by the quarter, half or litre is normal and usually the local wine the place actually drinks. Ordering it is not a downgrade — in an ordinary trattoria it is often the better call than the cheapest bottle on the list.

permissao: You are allowed to admit you do not know what something on the menu is. Scusi, cos'è questo gets an enthusiastic answer roughly every time — the dish nobody explains is the one you go home not having eaten.
espelho: Anyone who has ordered the one familiar item on a foreign menu four nights running knows exactly what this part costs to skip. It is not caution about food — it is the small effort of asking being higher than the effort of pointing at what you recognise.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You ask for a recommendation and the waiter names one dish immediately, with no alternatives offered.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: They are pushing whatever they need to sell tonight.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: A single confident answer usually means there is a right answer today — something that came in fresh, or the dish the kitchen is known for. A long list of options is the more commercial response, not the shorter one.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Take it, and say mi fido. If you genuinely cannot eat it, name the reason rather than asking for the list.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You eat the thing that place does best on the night you are there, which is not knowable from the menu at any price.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not in a place where the same recommendation is made to every table in four languages — there the confidence is a script, and the printed menu is the more honest document.
